s1.syndrome_frame: Painless vulvar mass with gradual enlargement
salient_findings: Painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region
Mass enlargement over the past four months
12cm, non-tender mass of the right labia majora
Well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass on soft-tissue ultrasound
key_facts: 67-year-old woman
Painless right vulvar mass
Mass first noted two years earlier
Gradual enlargement over the past four months
No pain, changes in appetite or bowel habits, urinary symptoms, weight loss, infection, or bleeding
Hypertension managed with valsartan/amlodipine
Hysterectomy in 2016 for abnormal uterine bleeding
Post-menopausal
No history of hormone therapy
Does not smoke or drink alcohol
Afebrile with normal vital signs
Abdominal exam unremarkable
12cm, non-tender mass of the right labia majora
No erythema, lymphadenopathy, or signs of inflammation
Pelvic exam otherwise normal
Soft-tissue ultrasound showed a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass
Mild peripheral blood flow on Doppler imaging
Routine laboratory results within normal limits

shortlist.label: Canal of Nuck hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the leading preoperative impression and the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Vulvar lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign tumor that could cause a painless vulvar mass

shortlist.label: Vulvar leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor that could cause a painless vulvar mass

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that could cause a painless vulvar mass with gradual enlargement

shortlist.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant tumor that could cause a vulvar mass, although less likely given the patient's lack of symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a painless, gradually enlarging vulvar mass extending into the inguinal region, along with ultrasound findings of a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass tracking into the inguinal canal, is consistent with a Canal of Nuck hernia, which is a rare hernia that occurs when tissue protrudes through a weak spot in the abdominal wall near the inguinal canal.

rejected.label: Vulvar lipoma
rejected.why: While possible, the mass's extension into the inguinal canal and the ultrasound description are less typical for a lipoma.

rejected.label: Vulvar leiomyoma
rejected.why: These are rare and the clinical and ultrasound findings do not specifically suggest a leiomyoma.

rejected.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a more rapid growth and possibly more symptoms due to its locally aggressive nature, which doesn't match the patient's gradual and asymptomatic presentation.

rejected.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
rejected.why: The lack of symptoms such as pain, infection, or bleeding, and the ultrasound description, make this diagnosis less likely compared to a Canal of Nuck hernia.
